title: QUETZAL: Vector Acceleration Framework for Modern Genome Sequence Analysis Algorithms
problem: CPU vector datapaths experience performance limitations for genome sequence analysis algorithms due to long-latency scatter/gather memory instructions when retrieving input sequence data. Fixed-function accelerators lack the generality to support diverse sequencing algorithms.
motivation: Genome sequence analysis is fundamental to medical breakthroughs including vaccine development, genome editing, and personalized medicine, but exponentially expanding datasets and algorithm complexity require significant performance enhancements.
method: QUETZAL is a hardware-software system that couples an accelerator to the CPU's vector processor using scratchpad buffers (fast local memory) and specialized vector instructions to speed up the slow process of gathering scattered pieces of genome sequence data from memory. It combines custom hardware and software to reduce these memory delays, pack more computation into single instructions, and quickly rearrange data representations as needed.
key_novelty: QUETZAL solves scatter-gather memory bottlenecks in CPU vector processors by tightly coupling an accelerator with scratchpad buffers and specialized vector instructions that work for any genomics algorithm.
contributions: First general-purpose vector acceleration framework applicable across diverse genome analysis algorithms
Hardware-software co-design with novel vector instructions to eliminate scatter/gather latency bottlenecks
Scratchpad buffer microarchitecture optimized for efficient genome sequence data access patterns
Support for multiple sequencing data formats and both short and long read types
limitations: Limitations are not discussed in the abstract.
